segments.narration: Hikers found a body that turned out to be 5000 years old. Nineteen ninety-one, the Ötztal Alps, sticking out of melting ice.
He came with his gear. A copper axe, a yew bow, a birch-bark container, and shoes stuffed with grass.
His skin carries sixty-one tattoos, mostly lines and crosses, and many sit over joints that show wear.
For ten years everyone assumed he froze. Then in two thousand and one an X-ray found a flint arrowhead in his left shoulder.
It had cut an artery. He bled out on that pass, and the ice kept the evidence for fifty-three centuries.

verdicts.claim: Ötzi was found in the Ötztal Alps in September 1991 and dates to roughly 3300 BCE
verdicts.note: Discovery was on 19 September 1991; radiocarbon dating gives c. 3350-3105 BCE.

verdicts.claim: Ötzi was found with equipment including a copper axe, a yew longbow and birch-bark containers
verdicts.note: 83% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: Ötzi's body bears 61 tattoos, largely simple lines and crosses positioned near worn joints
verdicts.note: Sixty-one tattoos have been catalogued, many over degenerated joints.

verdicts.claim: A 2001 X-ray revealed a flint arrowhead lodged in Ötzi's left shoulder
verdicts.note: The arrowhead was identified by radiology in 2001.

verdicts.claim: The arrow severed an artery and the resulting blood loss is considered the cause of death
verdicts.note: The wound to the left subclavian artery is accepted as the fatal injury.
